Agent.description:
A role-neutral participant in the scenario.

Agents reference existing scenario elements:

- ``entity`` links to the entities section (team/role) and supplies
  identity and role per ADR-020
- ``starting_accounts`` links to the accounts section
- ``allowed_subnets`` links to infrastructure entries
- ``initial_knowledge`` references nodes and infrastructure
- ``starting_assertions`` links to precondition assertions, giving the
  authoring surface a declarative hook for participant-relevant starting
  state without equating a probe implementation with truth (ACT-601)
- ``authority_anchors`` links to declared SDL elements (entities,
  relationships, content, etc.) that anchor what the participant is
  allowed or expected to do in scenario meaning (ACT-601, ADR-020)
- ``operating_scope`` links to targetable named scenario elements
  (subnets, hosts, services, content) defining where the participant
  may act or observe (ACT-601, ADR-020)
- ``observation_boundaries`` links to declared participant observation
  boundaries that define participant-specific projections of world and
  evidence state (SEM-208)
- ``interactive_access`` declares the compute-node/channel pairs that may be offered
  to this participant, without inferring a listener, locator, credential,
  operating scope, action authority, or successful realization (DSL-117)

Per ADR-073 the CybORG-inherited ``reward_calculator`` label was removed;
it was an unbound, unvalidated string and graded reward lives in the
experiment/evaluator plane (ADR-055/064/069).
Agent.title: Agent

RecordDomain.description:
Product structure: each declared field references another named domain.

``extra`` controls undeclared fields: ``False`` (closed) rejects any field not
named in ``fields``; ``True`` (open) admits them. Field values reference domain
names resolved against the envelope's ``domains`` map, keeping the structure
acyclic and free of inline recursion.
RecordDomain.title: RecordDomain

Relationship.description:
A typed directed edge between two named scenario elements.

Source and target can reference any named element in the scenario:
nodes, features, accounts, entities, or infrastructure entries.
The validator checks that both endpoints resolve.

The ``properties`` dict carries type-specific metadata (e.g.,
``trust_type: parent-child`` for AD trusts, ``protocol: SAML``
for federation). It's a flat dict rather than typed sub-models
because relationship properties vary widely and we don't want
to gate expressiveness on pre-modeling every variant.

``database_access`` and ``mail_access`` are typed exceptions where
protocol/auth details need structural validation rather than prose.
``forwarding_edge``, ``service_integration``, and ``proxy_upstream`` are
the same kind of typed exception for, respectively, a forwarding /
intel-sync agent's inter-node trust edge (SCN-010 §5.7), a platform
consumer-to-engine service integration, and a reverse-proxy/gateway
route-to-origin upstream hop. Each keeps protocol/auth/topology facts
structurally validated and cross-referable rather than buried in prose.
Relationship.title: Relationship

RelationshipDatabaseAccess.description:
Typed database-access detail carried by a top-level relationship edge.

When an application connects to a database, the relationship's ``target``
resolves to the database (service or logical database) and this block keeps
the ``role_ref`` (a ``role_id`` in that service) and ``auth_method``
structurally validated rather than recorded as prose (ADR-029 §4).
RelationshipDatabaseAccess.title: RelationshipDatabaseAccess

RelationshipDomainController.description: Typed marker for a node-to-domain controller-role edge.
RelationshipDomainController.title: RelationshipDomainController

RelationshipDomainJoin.description: Typed member join with explicit ordered controller candidates.
RelationshipDomainJoin.title: RelationshipDomainJoin

RelationshipForestTrust.description: Typed forest trust detail; relationship endpoints own forest identity.
RelationshipForestTrust.title: RelationshipForestTrust

RelationshipForwardingEdge.description:
Typed forwarding-trust detail carried by a top-level relationship edge.

The inter-node trust edge between a forwarding / intel-sync agent
(``forwarder_ref``, a ``forwarding_agent_id``) and the downstream consumer
it ships to. The consumer's transport listener is named by
``target_listener_role`` — REUSING the manager-side
``RuntimeSecurityMonitoringListenerRole`` lattice rather than forking a
parallel enum (SCN-010 §5.7).

The agent enrollment identity itself is never recorded: only the closed
``RuntimeForwardingEnrollmentClassification`` lattice (``none`` /
``redacted`` / ``operator_secret``). A present enrollment-identity ref must
classify ``redacted`` / ``operator_secret`` — a raw identity is never the
portable model.
RelationshipForwardingEdge.title: RelationshipForwardingEdge

RelationshipMailAccess.description: Typed mail-access detail carried by a top-level relationship edge.
RelationshipMailAccess.title: RelationshipMailAccess

RelationshipProxyUpstream.description:
Typed proxy-upstream detail carried by a top-level relationship edge.

When a reverse proxy / gateway forwards a route to an upstream origin, the
relationship's ``target`` resolves to that origin and this block keeps the
forwarding facts structurally validated rather than recorded as prose:
``route_ref`` (a ``route_id`` on the proxy's application surface), the
resolved upstream node/service, whether the client-facing TLS is terminated
at the proxy, whether the proxy-to-origin hop is plaintext, and any request
``body_limit`` the proxy enforces.
RelationshipProxyUpstream.title: RelationshipProxyUpstream

RelationshipServiceIntegration.description:
Typed service-integration detail carried by a top-level relationship edge.

When a consumer application integrates with a platform engine (analyzer,
responder, webhook, notification, or enrichment), the relationship's
endpoints resolve to the two platform applications and this block keeps the
``integration_kind``, ``auth_principal_ref`` (an ``app_authorization``
``principal_id`` in the target), and ``direction`` structurally validated
rather than recorded as prose. ``consumer_ref``/``engine_ref`` are the
``platform_application_id`` symbols of the two endpoints; a ``${var}``
placeholder is permitted in those refs.
RelationshipServiceIntegration.title: RelationshipServiceIntegration

RelationshipServiceIntegrationDirection.description:
Closed structural vocabulary for an integration edge's data direction.

Closed structural vocabulary: carries neither ``unknown`` nor ``other``.
RelationshipServiceIntegrationDirection.title: RelationshipServiceIntegrationDirection

RelationshipServiceIntegrationKind.description:
Open taxonomy of how a consumer integrates with a platform engine.

Open taxonomy: carries both ``unknown`` and ``other``.
RelationshipServiceIntegrationKind.title: RelationshipServiceIntegrationKind

RelationshipType.description: How two scenario elements relate to each other.
RelationshipType.title: RelationshipType

The raw credential value MUST NOT be recorded; the principal model has no

representation in the surface. Closed structural vocab: no ``unknown`` /
``other``.
RuntimeAppAuthorizationCredentialClassif.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationCredentialClassification

RuntimeAppAuthorizationGrant.description:
A resource-scoped permission grant (role -> actions -> resource pattern).

``resource_kind`` is the single author-settable source of truth for the

the declared set validated against these grants.
RuntimeAppAuthorizationGrant.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationGrant

RuntimeAppAuthorizationGrantEffect.description:
Closed allow/deny effect for a permission grant.

Closed structural vocab: no ``unknown`` / ``other``.
RuntimeAppAuthorizationGrantEffect.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationGrantEffect

RuntimeAppAuthorizationPrincipal.description:
A user, service account, API key, or backend role known to the store.

No raw secret is ever carried: the credential posture is recorded purely
via :attr:`credential_classification`.
RuntimeAppAuthorizationPrincipal.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationPrincipal

RuntimeAppAuthorizationPrincipalKind.description:

RuntimeAppAuthorizationPrincipalKind.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationPrincipalKind

RuntimeAppAuthorizationResourceVocabular.description:
Open spine discriminator for the resource space an RBAC store governs.

Tier placement (storage RBAC vs presentation RBAC) is derived from which
spine references the authorization, not declared here. Open taxonomy:
carries both ``unknown`` and ``other``.
RuntimeAppAuthorizationResourceVocabular.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationResourceVocabulary

RuntimeAppAuthorizationRole.description: A named role defined within the application authorization store.
RuntimeAppAuthorizationRole.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationRole

RuntimeAppAuthorizationRoleMapping.description: A mapping that binds backend roles, users, or hosts onto a local role.

RuntimeAppAuthorizationTenant.description: A tenant/namespace scope within the application authorization store.
RuntimeAppAuthorizationTenant.title: RuntimeAppAuthorizationTenant

RuntimeApplicationDisclosure.description:
Observable error or information-disclosure behavior of a route.

``disclosure`` is a classified description of what the application exposes
(a stack trace, an internal path, a backend version), never the raw payload,
token, password, or cookie itself.
RuntimeApplicationDisclosure.title: RuntimeApplicationDisclosure

RuntimeApplicationExposedField.description:
A route-visible fixture secret or intentionally exposed diagnostic field.

The sensitivity vocabulary is shared with the rest of the runtime surface.
A ``redacted`` or ``operator_secret`` field must omit its raw ``value``.
Other values, including credential-shaped fixture facts, are scenario
content needed for range realization and participant observation.
RuntimeApplicationExposedField.title: RuntimeApplicationExposedField

RuntimeApplicationParameter.description:
A typed request input observed on an application route.

``location`` distinguishes path variables, query string, headers, cookies,
form fields, JSON body fields, and uploaded-file fields.
RuntimeApplicationParameter.title: RuntimeApplicationParameter

RuntimeApplicationParameterLocation.description: Where a request input is carried on an observed route.
RuntimeApplicationParameterLocation.title: RuntimeApplicationParameterLocation

RuntimeApplicationProtocol.description: Application-layer protocol class for an observed application surface.
RuntimeApplicationProtocol.title: RuntimeApplicationProtocol

RuntimeApplicationRedirect.description:
An observed redirect a route can issue.

Target path/URL, status code, and the triggering condition are kept
distinct; the target is recorded verbatim, never resolved.
RuntimeApplicationRedirect.title: RuntimeApplicationRedirect

RuntimeApplicationResponse.description: An observed response a route can produce.
RuntimeApplicationResponse.title: RuntimeApplicationResponse

RuntimeApplicationRoute.description:
An observed application route — a participant-visible endpoint.

``route_id`` is the stable identity; ``path`` is data and may carry path
variables, may be shared across HTTP methods, and is never a mapping key.
RuntimeApplicationRoute.title: RuntimeApplicationRoute

RuntimeApplicationRouteUpstreamScheme.description:
Wire scheme a reverse proxy uses to reach a route's upstream origin.

This is a CLOSED taxonomy: an upstream is reached over either cleartext
HTTP or TLS-wrapped HTTPS. Unlike the open ``RuntimeApplicationProtocol``,
it carries neither ``other`` nor ``unknown`` — a proxy-to-origin hop that is
neither HTTP nor HTTPS is not an application route upstream.
RuntimeApplicationRouteUpstreamScheme.title: RuntimeApplicationRouteUpstreamScheme

RuntimeApplicationRouteUpstreamTarget.description:
The origin a reverse-proxied route forwards to.

A proxy/gateway route does not itself serve content; it relays to an
upstream origin on this or another node. ``target_node_ref`` /
``target_service`` name that origin (the service-name forms mirror
``RuntimeApplicationSurface.service``), ``scheme`` is the CLOSED
proxy-to-origin wire scheme, and ``tls_terminated_here`` records whether
TLS is terminated at the proxy (re-encrypted or plaintext to the origin).
All fields are observation metadata; nothing is resolved.
RuntimeApplicationRouteUpstreamTarget.title: RuntimeApplicationRouteUpstreamTarget

RuntimeApplicationSurface.description:
An observed application surface hosted by a transport service on a node.

``service`` references the owning same-node ``Node.services[].name`` (bare
name or the qualified ``nodes.<node>.services.<name>`` form). The surface is
observation metadata; it never mutates ``Node.services``.
RuntimeApplicationSurface.title: RuntimeApplicationSurface

RuntimeAptPackageRepository.description: Version 1 portable binary APT repository and dedicated trust binding.

uri.description: Credential-free HTTPS base URI of the binary APT repository.
uri.title: Uri

RuntimeAptPackageRepository.title: RuntimeAptPackageRepository

RuntimeCapabilityOverrideScope.description:
Scope of a ``RuntimeProcessCapabilityOverride``.

``PROCESS`` records a capability delta that applies only to the subject
process itself; ``SUBTREE`` records a delta that applies to the subject
process and every descendant it spawns (the motivating case is
``capsh --drop=cap_audit_control`` exec'ing ``sshd``, after which the
interactive shell subtree runs without ``CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL``).
RuntimeCapabilityOverrideScope.title: RuntimeCapabilityOverrideScope

RuntimeCapabilityPolicy.description: Linux/container capability policy observed for a runtime node.
RuntimeCapabilityPolicy.title: RuntimeCapabilityPolicy

RuntimeConfiguration.description:
Declarative runtime state required by a compute node.

Captured observations remain in evidence records unless an author
deliberately promotes the fact to one of these contract fields.
RuntimeConfiguration.title: RuntimeConfiguration

RuntimeContainerConfiguration.description: Required container runtime host and security configuration facts.
RuntimeContainerConfiguration.title: RuntimeContainerConfiguration

RuntimeControlInterface.description: A non-network local control API exposed inside a runtime node.
RuntimeControlInterface.title: RuntimeControlInterface

RuntimeControlInterfaceKind.description: Path-local control interface shape observed at runtime.
RuntimeControlInterfaceKind.title: RuntimeControlInterfaceKind

RuntimeDatabaseService.description:
An observed database service hosted by a transport service on a node.

``service`` references the owning same-node ``Node.services[].name`` (bare
name or the qualified ``nodes.<node>.services.<name>`` form). The inventory
is observation metadata; it never mutates ``Node.services``.
RuntimeDatabaseService.title: RuntimeDatabaseService

RuntimeDatastoreCluster.description:
The single observed cluster posture of a datastore service.

Captures the cluster-identity facts a search/wide-column cluster exposes:
native UUID, aggregate cardinality and size, shard totals, health,
discovery mode, partitioner, and native protocol version.
RuntimeDatastoreCluster.title: RuntimeDatastoreCluster

RuntimeDatastoreDataModel.description:
The logical data model of a datastore — the spine discriminator.

OPEN taxonomy (per the SCN-010 adversarial verdict): carries both
``unknown`` and ``other`` so an unrecognized model is permissive rather than
forcing a shallow relational encoding. ``document`` is intentionally absent —
no observed container realizes it (forbidden-completion discipline).
RuntimeDatastoreDataModel.title: RuntimeDatastoreDataModel

RuntimeDatastoreEngine.description:
Observed product family for a datastore service.

OPEN taxonomy: real-world datastore engines are unbounded, so both
``unknown`` and ``other`` are carried.
RuntimeDatastoreEngine.title: RuntimeDatastoreEngine

RuntimeDatastoreEnginePlugin.description:
An engine extension/plugin/module installed on a datastore node.

Per-node installed-capability inventory (OpenSearch plugins, Redis modules,
…). Carries the per-plugin ``version`` the name-only service-level list could
not. ``plugin_id`` is a stable symbol; ``name`` is the observed engine name.
RuntimeDatastoreEnginePlugin.title: RuntimeDatastoreEnginePlugin

RuntimeDatastoreEvictionPolicy.description:
A key-value eviction policy.

OPEN taxonomy: carries both ``unknown`` and ``other``. Covers Redis
``maxmemory-policy`` values.
RuntimeDatastoreEvictionPolicy.title: RuntimeDatastoreEvictionPolicy

RuntimeDatastoreMapping.description:
A bounded manifest of an observed search-index mapping/schema.

Carries schema geometry and digest/evidence facts, never the raw
OpenSearch/Elasticsearch ``_mapping`` response body.
RuntimeDatastoreMapping.title: RuntimeDatastoreMapping

RuntimeDatastoreNode.description:
An observed node participating in a datastore cluster.

Beyond cluster membership and roles, a node carries product-neutral engine
provenance (version, build hash/type), JVM/process memory posture (initial
and maximum heap byte bounds, memory-lock state), a typed per-node engine
plugin inventory, and typed published endpoints (client vs peer listeners).
All are observed runtime facts — never host policy or software-component
identity (ADR-058 amending ADR-048).
RuntimeDatastoreNode.title: RuntimeDatastoreNode

RuntimeDatastoreNodeEndpoint.description:
An observed published listener on a datastore node.

Product-neutral node listener topology: ``role`` distinguishes the
participant-facing ``client`` listener from the inter-node ``peer`` listener
without encoding engine-native names. ``address`` and ``port`` stay split,
matching every other runtime listener surface. A node endpoint records
published topology, not proof of an OS bind or host publication (ADR-058).
RuntimeDatastoreNodeEndpoint.title: RuntimeDatastoreNodeEndpoint

RuntimeDatastoreNodeEndpointRole.description:
The role a datastore node's published listener fulfils.

OPEN taxonomy: carries both ``unknown`` and ``other``. ``client`` is the
participant/application-facing listener (OpenSearch ``http``, Cassandra
native/CQL, Redis client); ``peer`` is the inter-node/cluster listener
(OpenSearch ``transport``, Cassandra internode, Redis cluster-bus).
Engine-native listener names are intentionally not modelled — the datastore
spine stays product-neutral (ADR-048, ADR-058).
RuntimeDatastoreNodeEndpointRole.title: RuntimeDatastoreNodeEndpointRole

RuntimeDatastoreNodeRole.description:
A role a cluster node fulfils.

OPEN taxonomy: carries both ``unknown`` and ``other``. Covers OpenSearch
``cluster_manager``/``data``/``ingest``/``ml`` roles and Cassandra
``coordinator``/``seed`` roles uniformly.
RuntimeDatastoreNodeRole.title: RuntimeDatastoreNodeRole

RuntimeDatastorePartition.description:
An observed partition primitive (index / keyspace / logical_db / family).

Carries the geometry that differentiates one datastore data model from
another: native partition/index UUID, shard/replica and document counts for
a search index, replication strategy + factor + per-DC factor map for a
wide-column keyspace, and a datatype census for a key-value logical
database.
RuntimeDatastorePartition.title: RuntimeDatastorePartition

RuntimeDatastorePartitionKind.description:
The kind of a datastore partition/namespace primitive.

OPEN taxonomy: carries both ``unknown`` and ``other``. An ``index`` is the
search-cluster primary object, a ``keyspace`` the wide-column one, a
``logical_db`` a numbered key-value database, and a ``column_family`` a
wide-column table.
RuntimeDatastorePartitionKind.title: RuntimeDatastorePartitionKind

RuntimeDatastorePersistence.description:
The single observed persistence posture of a key-value datastore.

Captures Redis-style persistence: RDB save points, AOF on/off, the eviction
policy, and the maxmemory ceiling. Its presence is the defining profile a
``key_value`` data model must carry.
RuntimeDatastorePersistence.title: RuntimeDatastorePersistence

RuntimeDatastoreReplicationStrategy.description:
A wide-column replication strategy — the spine discriminator's geometry.

OPEN taxonomy (per the SCN-010 verdict): carries both ``unknown`` and
``other``. Covers Cassandra ``SimpleStrategy``/``NetworkTopologyStrategy``.
RuntimeDatastoreReplicationStrategy.title: RuntimeDatastoreReplicationStrategy

RuntimeDatastoreService.description:
An observed datastore service hosted by a transport service on a node.

The single non-relational datastore spine. ``service`` references the owning
same-node ``Node.services[].name`` (bare name or the qualified
``nodes.<node>.services.<name>`` form). The ``data_model`` discriminator
selects the required profile the ``require_profile_for_data_model`` guard
enforces.
RuntimeDatastoreService.title: RuntimeDatastoreService

RuntimeDatastoreSetting.description:
An observed datastore runtime setting with scope, provenance, and class.

Explicit ``redacted`` / ``operator_secret`` classifications omit raw values;
names that look credential-bearing remain scenario content unless the
author marks the value withheld.
RuntimeDatastoreSetting.title: RuntimeDatastoreSetting

RuntimeDatastoreSettingProvenance.description:
Where an observed datastore runtime setting value came from.

OPEN taxonomy: provenance sources are extensible, so both ``unknown`` and
``other`` are carried (mirrors ``DatabaseSettingProvenance``).
RuntimeDatastoreSettingProvenance.title: RuntimeDatastoreSettingProvenance

RuntimeDatastoreSettingScope.description:
The scope a datastore runtime setting applies at.

CLOSED structural vocab: the scope lattice (cluster / node / partition /
engine) is fixed by the spine's own topology, so no ``unknown`` / ``other``.
RuntimeDatastoreSettingScope.title: RuntimeDatastoreSettingScope

RuntimeDatastoreTemplate.description:
A bounded manifest of an observed index template body.

The template captures patterns, selected settings, optional mapping linkage,
digest, and evidence refs without embedding the backend's raw template JSON.
RuntimeDatastoreTemplate.title: RuntimeDatastoreTemplate

RuntimeDatastoreTransportSecurity.description:
The single observed transport-security posture of a datastore service.

Records the intra-cluster transport TLS mode and whether client/node
certificate verification is enforced — the observable ``xpack.security`` /
``SKIPSSL_VERIFY`` posture, never the certificate material itself.
RuntimeDatastoreTransportSecurity.title: RuntimeDatastoreTransportSecurity

RuntimeDatastoreTransportSecurityMode.description:
The transport-security posture of a datastore service.

CLOSED structural vocab: the observable TLS posture is a fixed three-way
distinction (none / one-way TLS / mutual TLS), so no ``unknown`` / ``other``.
A ``${var}`` placeholder remains expressible at the field level.
RuntimeDatastoreTransportSecurityMode.title: RuntimeDatastoreTransportSecurityMode

RuntimeDependencyManifest.description: A dependency manifest required in the runtime artifact.
RuntimeDependencyManifest.title: RuntimeDependencyManifest

RuntimeDeviceMapping.description: A host device mapping required in runtime configuration.
RuntimeDeviceMapping.title: RuntimeDeviceMapping

RuntimeDnsService.description: An observed DNS service hosted by a node.
RuntimeDnsService.title: RuntimeDnsService

RuntimeEnvironmentFile.description:
A node runtime env-file delivered from a generated-artifact output.

The file is an opaque generated-artifact output projected as one runtime
environment input; RAES does not parse or compare its individual key/value
entries. Authors declare the binding here, on the node, not as a fake
variable name and not as an ordinary read-only file mount.

``name`` is a bounded portable identity, not a filesystem path: the compiler
forwards it as the env-file target in the provisioning projection, so it must
not admit path traversal, newlines, or shell metacharacters that could
redirect the generated secret outside the runtime env-file namespace.
RuntimeEnvironmentFile.title: RuntimeEnvironmentFile

RuntimeEnvironmentValueClassification.description: Sensitivity classification for a required runtime environment value.
RuntimeEnvironmentValueClassification.title: RuntimeEnvironmentValueClassification

RuntimeEnvironmentVariable.description: Required runtime environment variable with provenance and sensitivity.
RuntimeEnvironmentVariable.title: RuntimeEnvironmentVariable

RuntimeEnvironmentVariableProvenance.description: Required origin class for a runtime environment variable.
RuntimeEnvironmentVariableProvenance.title: RuntimeEnvironmentVariableProvenance

RuntimeExtraHost.description: A required extra host mapping in runtime configuration.
RuntimeExtraHost.title: RuntimeExtraHost

RuntimeFileService.description:
A node-scoped runtime file-service inventory.

``service`` references the owning same-node ``Node.services[].name``
(bare name or qualified ``nodes.<node>.services.<name>``).
RuntimeFileService.title: RuntimeFileService

RuntimeFileServiceAccessAction.description: Portable action vocabulary for file-service access policy/observations.
RuntimeFileServiceAccessAction.title: RuntimeFileServiceAccessAction

RuntimeFileServiceAccessBasis.description: Basis/provenance for an access claim or observation.
RuntimeFileServiceAccessBasis.title: RuntimeFileServiceAccessBasis

RuntimeFileServiceAccessEffect.description: Portable effect for an authored or computed file-service access rule.
RuntimeFileServiceAccessEffect.title: RuntimeFileServiceAccessEffect

RuntimeFileServiceAccessObservation.description:
An observed probe outcome against a file-service resource.

Observations are evidence; they support but do not overwrite authored
or configured policy.
RuntimeFileServiceAccessObservation.title: RuntimeFileServiceAccessObservation

RuntimeFileServiceAccessOutcome.description: Observed outcome class for a per-share access probe.
RuntimeFileServiceAccessOutcome.title: RuntimeFileServiceAccessOutcome

RuntimeFileServiceAccessRule.description: An authored or computed access rule for a file-service resource.
RuntimeFileServiceAccessRule.title: RuntimeFileServiceAccessRule

RuntimeFileServiceCredentialClassificati.description:
Semantic classification of a service-local credential.

The raw credential value MUST NOT be recorded; the principal model
has no field that can hold one. This vocabulary is the only credential
representation in the file-service surface — it describes the
strength/posture of the credential as observed (or its absence) so
downstream consumers can reason about exposure without leaking secret
material into fixtures, schemas, diagnostics, or logs.
RuntimeFileServiceCredentialClassificati.title: RuntimeFileServiceCredentialClassification

RuntimeFileServicePrincipal.description:
A service-local principal (Samba passdb-style account or group).

Service-local principals are NOT promoted to top-level ``accounts``,
``runtime.local_identity``, or ``runtime.identity_authorities``.
Optional ``local_user_ref`` and ``directory_subject_ref`` carry refs to
those surfaces when a mapping is observed.

Raw credential material (passwords, NT/LM hashes, Kerberos keys, private
keys, bearer tokens, captured credentials) is unrepresentable on this
record per ADR-037 §4 and the secret-handling gate; only
``credential_classification`` is carried, so the field surface itself
cannot smuggle a secret into models, schemas, fixtures, diagnostics, or
snapshots.
RuntimeFileServicePrincipal.title: RuntimeFileServicePrincipal

RuntimeFileServicePrincipalKind.description: Portable kind of a service-local principal in a file service.
RuntimeFileServicePrincipalKind.title: RuntimeFileServicePrincipalKind

RuntimeFileServicePrincipalOrigin.description: Origin/provenance class for a service-local principal record.
RuntimeFileServicePrincipalOrigin.title: RuntimeFileServicePrincipalOrigin

RuntimeFileServicePrincipalStatus.description: Observed account status for a service-local principal.
RuntimeFileServicePrincipalStatus.title: RuntimeFileServicePrincipalStatus

RuntimeFileServiceProtocol.description: Portable protocol family for an observed runtime file service.
RuntimeFileServiceProtocol.title: RuntimeFileServiceProtocol

RuntimeFileServiceShare.description: A published share/resource on a runtime file service.
RuntimeFileServiceShare.title: RuntimeFileServiceShare

RuntimeFileShareKind.description: Observed kind of a published file-service share/resource.
RuntimeFileShareKind.title: RuntimeFileShareKind

RuntimeFilesystemEntry.description: A filesystem entry observed inside a runtime node or container asset.
RuntimeFilesystemEntry.title: RuntimeFilesystemEntry

RuntimeFilesystemEntryType.description: Observed type of a runtime filesystem inventory entry.
RuntimeFilesystemEntryType.title: RuntimeFilesystemEntryType

RuntimeFilesystemPresence.description:
Observed presence state for a runtime filesystem inventory entry.

``present`` is the default and preserves prior behavior. ``expected_absent``
records an authored or expected path that was not observed at capture time —
for example a deploy-key path attempted by setup code but missing in the
captured steady state. Absent entries retain their expected ``entry_type``
instead of collapsing to ``other``; present-only facts (size, content
digest, owner ids, mode) must be omitted, per ADR-037.
RuntimeFilesystemPresence.title: RuntimeFilesystemPresence

RuntimeFilesystemStability.description: Stability class for an observed runtime filesystem or mount fact.
RuntimeFilesystemStability.title: RuntimeFilesystemStability

RuntimeForwardingAgent.description:
Node-scoped runtime inventory for a forwarding / intel-sync agent.

The single forwarder spine. The ``agent_kind`` discriminator selects the
required profile the ``require_profile_for_agent_kind`` guard enforces.
Cadence composes a ``runtime.scheduled_jobs`` entry; the inter-node trust
edge composes a ``RelationshipForwardingEdge`` — neither is re-typed here.
RuntimeForwardingAgent.title: RuntimeForwardingAgent

RuntimeForwardingAgentImplementation.description: Observed product family for a forwarding / intel-sync agent (OPEN).
RuntimeForwardingAgentImplementation.title: RuntimeForwardingAgentImplementation

RuntimeForwardingAgentKind.description: Portable forwarding-agent role discriminator (OPEN per the verdict).
RuntimeForwardingAgentKind.title: RuntimeForwardingAgentKind

RuntimeForwardingAgentOwnershipRole.description: Closed ownership of an agent relative to the system under test.
RuntimeForwardingAgentOwnershipRole.title: RuntimeForwardingAgentOwnershipRole

RuntimeForwardingBufferCrypto.description: Portable at-rest / in-transit crypto of a buffer policy (OPEN).
RuntimeForwardingBufferCrypto.title: RuntimeForwardingBufferCrypto

RuntimeForwardingBufferPolicy.description:
The single observed buffer / back-pressure posture of a forwarder.

Captures the ``client_buffer`` shape: queue capacity, events-per-second
ceiling, at-rest/in-transit crypto, and reconnect interval. Its presence is
the defining profile a ``log_forwarder`` must carry.
RuntimeForwardingBufferPolicy.title: RuntimeForwardingBufferPolicy

RuntimeForwardingEnrollmentClassificatio.description:
Redaction class for a ship-target enrollment identity (CLOSED).

A fixed structural lattice — an enrollment credential is either absent
(``none``) or present-but-not-recorded (``redacted`` / ``operator_secret``).
Raw enrollment-key material is never carried; per the enum-sentinel
discipline this closed set carries no ``unknown`` / ``other`` tail.
RuntimeForwardingEnrollmentClassificatio.title: RuntimeForwardingEnrollmentClassification

RuntimeForwardingParseFormat.description: Portable on-the-wire / on-disk parse format of a source (OPEN).

SshForcedCommand.description:
A typed sshd ``ForceCommand`` configuration.

The ``command_kind`` discriminates how ``command`` is interpreted:

- ``absolute_path``: a concrete executable path (or ``${var}``) starting
  with ``/``. Validated via ``absolute_path_or_var``.
- ``internal_sftp``: the sshd-internal sftp subsystem; ``command`` must
  equal the literal ``"internal-sftp"``.
- ``redacted``: the underlying command is withheld from the SDL model
  because it carries secrets, session identifiers, or operator-only
  arguments; ``command`` must be empty and ``command_redacted`` must
  be true.

(wildcards, comma-separated lists) and is not cross-checked.

is two). Per-rule sshd directives override the surrounding global
directives for sessions that match all listed criteria.
